memory_update.text: AMKR should remain a reference anchor for US-listed advanced packaging/OSAT overflow capacity, but later layers must verify AI/HPC customer mix and capacity qualification rather than assuming all advanced packaging is AI-relevant.
ONTO and ACMR are better underfollowed equipment/process-tool mappings for FOPLP and panel-level packaging than mega-cap semiconductor equipment leaders in this pass.
KLIC is a focused CPO/silicon-photonics bonding-equipment candidate; survival to Layer 2 depends on proving production-scale CPO orders, not only development-tool wins.

Need a follow-up search for US-listed materials and components tied to redistribution layers, temporary bonding/debonding, glass-core substrates, thermal interface materials, and optical-engine attach; current pass is equipment/OSAT-heavy.

node: Advanced packaging, fan-out panel-level packaging, and co-packaged optics integration
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the AI advanced-packaging/FOPLP/CPO node finds one reference OSAT anchor and three underfollowed equipment/process-tool names. The strongest direct public-market mapping is Amkor as a US-listed advanced packaging and test provider tied to US onshoring and AI chip packaging capacity. The more underfollowed discovery lane is in process control, panel lithography, plating, wet processing, and thermocompression bonding tools that may become chokepoints if fan-out panel-level packaging and co-packaged optics scale beyond pilot lines. These are research candidates only, not investment recommendations.
